LLM_description:
Situation:
A high-impact storm has disrupted the coastal and inland districts. Primary corridors are degraded by flooding and landslides; several bridges are load-restricted; and security along the valley approaches remains uncertain. Regional Supply Depot Alpha (near the airhead), Supply Depot Bravo (port complex), and Forward Logistics Base Charlie (inland) hold mixed stocks of potable water, emergency rations, medical materiel, and shelter items. Requests for immediate resupply have been received from North Relief Battalion (Sector North), Field Hospital Delta, IDP Camp Horizon, Community Support Hub Echo, and Civil Defense Company Foxtrot. Movement is constrained by curfews, daylight-only convoy windows, and the need for armed escort or route clearance in contested areas.

Mission:
Deliver life-sustaining commodities from the depots to the designated receiving units across the next operational periods while minimizing total operational cost. Cost elements include transport, controlled shortfall penalties, vehicle deployment, and fixed security risk costs for route activation.

Execution/Concept:
- Priorities: Stabilize clinical operations and potable water access first, then sustain food and shelter. Shortfalls are allowed only as a last resort and will incur specified penalties to reflect humanitarian impact or emergency local procurement.
- Allocation: Shipments will be pushed from each depot within daily stock limits. All cargo is planned by commodity-specific volume factors to ensure each vehicle is utilized within capacity. Transport costs vary by depot-to-unit corridor; where multiple corridors exist, the lowest-cost and safest option will be preferred.
- Route activation and risk: Any corridor used on a given day must be formally activated. Activating a route (sending any vehicles) incurs a fixed Risk Cost that represents escorts, route clearance, and security overwatch, regardless of the number of vehicles dispatched on that route that day. Additional vehicles on an already activated route do not add to this fixed component, but still incur per-vehicle and transport costs. Where risk exposure is elevated, route activation will be minimized by consolidating loads.
- Vehicle employment: Each vehicle deployed incurs a cost and cannot exceed the capacity limit. Vehicles are assigned to specific depot-to-unit movements by day. The total fleet available per day cannot be exceeded; routes cannot carry vehicles unless activated.
- Stocks and demand: Outflows from each depot are capped by available stocks by commodity and day. Receiving units have minimum daily demand by commodity; any unmet portion is captured as controlled shortfall subject to penalty. Deliveries may be split across depots to meet demand where feasible.
- Phasing and flexibility: Plans will be updated each period to reflect changing access, security, and receipt of new stocks. Movement Control will coordinate convoy timing with security forces and civil authorities to avoid curfew violations and deconflict with engineering teams. Alternate corridors will be considered when primary routes are disrupted, with their associated transport and risk costs.
